issues.description: getSourceMap reads and parses files on every stack frame with no caching
issues.detail: For each frame in an external module, the code calls existsSync + readFileSync + convertSourceMap.fromSource. A single stack trace with N frames in the same file pays N file reads and N parses. The value (the source map) is being recomputed per frame when it is a stable fact about the file. Memoize by file path.

issues.description: resolve(from, '..', s) silently changes path semantics and is undocumented
issues.detail: The fix changes resolve(s, from) to resolve(from, '..', s || ''). That is a meaningful semantic shift: sources are now resolved relative to the directory of `from`, not against `from` itself. This is probably correct, but the code complects 'where the map lives' with 'where its sources live' without a comment naming the time/identity of `from`. A one-line note would prevent the next regression.

issues.description: Module presence check complects 'is external' with 'has no transformResult'
issues.detail: The heuristic `!mod?.transformResult && existsSync(file)` is being asked to mean 'this is an external module Vite did not transform.' That's three concerns intertwined: module identity, transform state, and filesystem existence. When Vite's internals change what transformResult holds, this silently degrades. Extract an `isExternalUntransformed(file)` predicate and state the assumption.

issues.description: createConvertSourceMapReadMap returns '{}' as a fallback source map
issues.detail: When the referenced map file does not exist, the reader returns the string '{}' to 'avoid errors'. That swallows a real signal (broken sourcemap reference) into a value that looks valid. Either return undefined and let the caller decide, or log once. Silent fallbacks are place-oriented thinking: a hidden state that no one sees.

issues.description: New convert-source-map dependency duplicates capability already in @jridgewell/trace-mapping
issues.detail: The project already depends on @jridgewell/trace-mapping (used in DecodedMap) and the broader jridgewell toolset can parse inline and file-referenced sourcemaps. Adding convert-source-map adds a second mental model for the same value (a parsed source map) in the same package. Worth a sentence in the PR on why the existing toolchain could not do this.

issues.description: extractSourcemapFromFile is copied from Vite without an abstraction boundary
issues.detail: The comment 'based on vite' links a commit SHA and inlines the logic. That is two copies of the same behavior with no shared identity. When Vite's version evolves (it will), this one will drift silently. Either import from Vite if exposed, or name the divergence explicitly so a future reader knows this is a fork, not a snapshot.

review.summary: The fix addresses a real problem — external module stack frames were not getting source-map resolution — but it does so by complecting several concerns in test-run.ts: external-module detection, transformResult inspection, filesystem existence, and per-frame I/O. The getSourceMap callback recomputes a stable value (a file's source map) per frame with no memoization, which is place-oriented thinking dressed as a closure. The resolve() change in source-map.ts is probably the right semantics but is undocumented and easy to regress. A new dependency (convert-source-map) is introduced alongside the existing jridgewell toolchain without a stated reason for the duplication. None of this is wrong enough to block, but the design has not been decomposed: pull out a memoized sourcemap-for-file function, name the external-module predicate, and the code becomes simple rather than just working.
